items.title: A morphism from an affine scheme is quasi-affine exactly when it is quasi-compact
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter morphisms.tex (Morphisms of Schemes)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file morphisms.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma says that for an affine source a morphism is quasi-affine exactly when it is quasi-compact, so in particular every morphism from an affine scheme to a quasi-separated scheme is quasi-affine (statement lines 2358-2364). The counted proof is short and complete: it reduces to the preimage of an affine open of the target, which is an open subscheme of the affine source and hence quasi-affine exactly when quasi-compact, and then deduces the particular case by applying the permanence statement for quasi-compactness to the composite with the structure morphism (proof lines 2366-2373). It is H2: both steps are carried out in the counted span, with the cited input being the permanence statement for quasi-compact morphisms.
